data.one_liner: Detects the running platform, browser type, and operating system with utility widgets.
data.what_it_does: Identifies the platform (web, mobile, desktop, mobile browser, desktop browser) on which a Flutter application is running. Provides utility methods, conditional check functions, and widgets to render platform-specific UI.
use_when: You need to conditionally render different UI components based on whether the app runs on a mobile device, web, or desktop.
You need to detect browser-specific environments like Web Android or Web iOS.
avoid_when: You only need standard Flutter platform checks available out of the box via targetPlatform.
You are writing non-Flutter Dart code.
strengths: Provides fine-grained detection including mobile vs desktop browsers.
Includes helpful widgets like PlatformDetectByType and PlatformDetectByName for declarative rendering.
weaknesses: Relies on universal_html which might add unnecessary dependencies if web browser detection is not needed.
Duplicates functionality that can be achieved via Flutter's core libraries and universal_platform.
data.setup_notes: Add the dependency to pubspec.yaml and import the library.

alternatives.name: universal_platform
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you just need standard platform detection across web and native platforms without extra UI widgets.
